expressions.suspect:countess_morvaine: Countess Morvaine received the inspector in the mirror gallery with her gloves on. Her voice carried the cadence of someone accustomed to being believed.
expressions.event:balcony_fall: Luca Marini fell from the main balcony onto the courtyard flagstones. The railing showed score marks where the stone had been weakened.
expressions.motive:forgery_operation: Fourteen paintings in the Contarini collection had been replaced with forgeries over six years. The originals were sold privately through a dealer in Zurich.
expressions.suspect:carlo_bassi: Carlo Bassi arrived by gondola at half past nine wearing a white silk mask. His invitation was addressed to the previous owner of his seat.
expressions.suspect:dr_klaus_winter: Dr Klaus Winter examined the collection as an independent appraiser. His report on the Titian was due at the insurance office by Friday.
expressions.suspect:elena_rizzoli: Elena Rizzoli managed the palazzo's exhibition schedule and private sales. Her commission on the last three auctions exceeded her annual salary.
expressions.suspect:marco_dandolo: Marco Dandolo waited in the courtyard after the masks were removed at midnight. His glove was torn at the palm and he offered no explanation.
expressions.suspect:signora_pelosi: Signora Pelosi kept the palazzo keys and managed the household. She had worked for the Contarini family before the Countess acquired the property.
expressions.suspect:inspector_bruno: Inspector Bruno arrived from the cultural crimes division at dawn. He had investigated the Countess once before, in connection with a sale in Milan.
expressions.location:palazzo_contarini: Palazzo Contarini faces the Grand Canal with a facade of pink stone. The carnival lanterns still burned when the body was found at dawn.
expressions.location:main_balcony: The main balcony overlooks the courtyard from the second floor. The stone railing is original to the building and shows deep score marks at one joint.
expressions.location:mirror_gallery: The mirror gallery runs the length of the piano nobile between gilded frames. Fourteen paintings hang on the east wall, each with a provenance card.
expressions.location:canal_entrance: The canal entrance admits guests by water through an arched gate. A bronze key locks the gate from inside after the last gondola.
expressions.location:studio_room: The studio room on the third floor served as Marini's workspace during the restoration. His brushes were still wet when the room was sealed.
expressions.location:servants_stair: The servants' stair connects the kitchen to the upper floors without passing the gallery. The door at each landing bolts from the stair side.
expressions.location:courtyard: The courtyard is paved in Istrian stone and open to the sky. Marini's body lay at the base of the balcony, ten feet from the well.
expressions.location:private_salon: The private salon adjoins the gallery and is used for viewings. An auction catalogue lay open on the console beside two champagne glasses.
expressions.object:cracked_mirror: A mirror in the gallery shows a hairline crack running from corner to corner. The crack was not present in the previous season's photographs.
expressions.object:paint_analysis: A paint analysis of the Titian reveals cadmium yellow, a pigment not available before 1820. The painting is dated 1560.
expressions.object:forged_canvas: A canvas in the studio room matches the dimensions of the missing Bellini. The stretcher bars are new but the linen has been artificially aged.
expressions.object:balcony_railing: The balcony railing broke at a joint where the stone had been scored. The cut is straight and made with a masonry tool.
expressions.object:guest_list: The guest list for the carnival reception shows forty-two names. The Countess added three by hand after the invitations were printed.
expressions.object:provenance_file: The provenance file for each painting traces ownership to a private collection in Vienna. Two of the chains of ownership share a fictional dealer.
expressions.object:pigment_sample: A pigment scraping from the gallery Titian contains zinc white and synthetic ultramarine. Both substances postdate the supposed creation by three centuries.
expressions.object:silk_glove: A white silk glove was found on the balcony floor. The fabric matches the pair worn by Carlo Bassi at the reception.
expressions.object:auction_catalogue: The auction catalogue lists eight works from the Contarini collection. The estimated value of the lot exceeds four million euros.
expressions.object:restoration_notes: Marini's restoration notes describe inconsistencies in the paint layers of three works. His final entry reads not original, crossed out and rewritten.
expressions.object:canal_key: The bronze canal key was found in Signora Pelosi's apron pocket. The lock it opens was oiled recently and the mechanism turns without sound.
expressions.object:linen_fragment: A fragment of old linen was found in the studio waste bin. The weave matches a type manufactured in Belgium in the 1920s.
expressions.object:sale_receipt: A Zurich sale receipt records a Bellini purchased for over one million euros. The listed buyer is a known alias.
expressions.emotion:polished_grace: She poured coffee for the inspector without being asked. Her hand was steady and her posture did not shift when the forgeries were mentioned.
expressions.emotion:startled_poise: He set down his glass too quickly when the balcony was mentioned. The wine spilled and he wiped it with his glove.
expressions.emotion:measured_deflection: Each question about the paintings was answered with a reference to the provenance file. She never addressed the pigment analysis directly.
expressions.emotion:stiff_formality: Signora Pelosi stood with her hands clasped and answered in formal Italian. She addressed the Countess as 'la Contessa' even when speaking about the body.
expressions.emotion:avoided_subject: He changed the subject twice when the Zurich dealer was named. His notebook remained closed throughout the interview.
expressions.emotion:practised_dismay: She pressed a hand to her chest and said 'how terrible' in precisely measured tones. Her earrings did not swing.
expressions.modifier:railing_scored: The stone railing was scored along a horizontal line at the weakest joint. The cut reduced the load capacity to a fraction of its original strength.
expressions.modifier:modern_pigment: The pigment analysis found materials manufactured after 1900 in a painting attributed to the sixteenth century. The discrepancy is conclusive.
expressions.modifier:frame_swapped: The frame on the gallery Bellini does not match the catalogue photograph from three years ago. The gilding pattern differs at the lower left corner.
expressions.modifier:carnival_mask: Carnival masks were worn by all guests until midnight. After the unmasking, the balcony was accessible from the gallery stair.
expressions.modifier:door_bolted: The servants' stair door on the second floor was bolted from inside when checked at dawn. Someone used it and re-bolted it before leaving.
expressions.modifier:canvas_aged: The studio canvas had been treated with tea and varnish to simulate age. Under ultraviolet light, the treatment is clearly visible.
expressions.modifier:varnish_fresh: Fresh varnish was applied to two gallery paintings within the past month. The varnish conceals surface irregularities visible in earlier photographs.
expressions.modifier:scratch_on_stone: A scratch on the courtyard flagstone extends from the base of the balcony outward. The mark is consistent with a falling body striking stone.
expressions.modifier:glove_torn: The torn glove matches a pair sold by a single Venetian glovemaker. Carlo Bassi and Countess Morvaine both patronise this shop.
expressions.modifier:silk_residue: A trace of silk fibre was found on the balcony railing near the break point. The fibre matches the weave of the Countess's evening wrap.
expressions.action:canvas_switched: The original Bellini was removed from its frame and replaced with a copy. The switch was made in the studio room on the third floor.
expressions.action:railing_weakened: The balcony railing was scored with a masonry chisel along its weakest joint. The work required fewer than ten minutes.
expressions.action:studio_locked: The studio room was locked after the fall and the key was not found. Signora Pelosi stated she had not entered since the previous afternoon.
expressions.action:mask_removed: Masks were removed at midnight as is carnival custom. After the unmasking, guests moved freely between the gallery and the balcony.
expressions.action:notes_destroyed: Marini's final restoration report was removed from the studio desk. Only the working notes in his notebook survived.
expressions.action:sale_arranged: The sale of four paintings was arranged privately through a Zurich intermediary. The receipts were kept in a locked drawer in the private salon.
expressions.action:provenance_forged: The provenance documents for the replaced paintings were fabricated using aged paper and period-appropriate ink. One signature was traced from a genuine document.
expressions.action:stair_descended: Someone descended the servants' stair between midnight and one. The maid heard footsteps but saw no one when she checked the landing.
expressions.action:gallery_inspected: Dr Winter inspected the gallery collection during the reception interval. He requested a pigment sample from the Titian and was refused.
expressions.time:carnival_evening: The carnival reception began at nine and guests arrived by gondola. Masks were worn until midnight and the balcony was open from ten.
expressions.time:midnight_bell: The midnight bell marked the unmasking. By half past twelve the gallery was empty and only the Countess remained on the upper floor.
expressions.time:body_found_dawn: The palazzo maid found Marini's body in the courtyard at first light. The carnival lanterns had burned down to stubs.
expressions.time:gallery_closed: The gallery was closed to visitors at eleven for the private reception. The studio room was last accessed at half past ten.
expressions.time:auction_date: The auction was scheduled for the following month in Zurich. The catalogue had already been printed and distributed to collectors.
expressions.motive:collection_value: The forged collection was insured for twelve million euros. If the originals were discovered to be copies, the insurance claim would constitute fraud.
expressions.motive:exposure_risk: Marini's restoration notes identified the forgeries conclusively. His report to the conservation committee would have triggered an investigation.
expressions.motive:rival_claim: Signora Pelosi's late employer had disputed the Countess's purchase of the palazzo. The property claim was settled but the resentment remained.
expressions.motive:insurance_fraud: Elena Rizzoli stood to earn a commission on the Zurich auction. If the forgeries were exposed before the sale, she would face criminal charges.
expressions.motive:reputation_ruin: The Countess had built her social position on the collection. Exposure as a forger would end her standing in Venice and beyond.
expressions.witness:gondolier: The gondolier brought the last guest at half past eleven. He waited at the canal entrance until one and saw no one leave by water.
expressions.witness:palazzo_maid: The palazzo maid heard footsteps on the servants' stair after midnight. She found the courtyard door unbolted at dawn.
expressions.witness:night_guard: The night guard patrolled the courtyard at midnight and again at three. He did not look up at the balcony on either round.
expressions.witness:art_dealer: The art dealer from Zurich spoke with the Countess during the reception. He confirmed that four paintings were reserved for the spring auction.
expressions.witness:canal_boatman: A canal boatman saw a light in the studio window at half past one. The light went out after several minutes and did not return.
expressions.event:luca_marini_discovered: Luca Marini was found in the courtyard below the main balcony at dawn. His restoration notebook lay open beside him on the stone.
expressions.event:carnival_reception: The carnival reception drew forty guests to the piano nobile. Champagne was served and the gallery was open for a private viewing.
